'''Faheem Hussain''' (31 July 1942 – 29 September 2009), was a [[Pakistani people|Pakistani]] [[theoretical physicist]] and a professor of [[physics]] at the [[Lahore University of Management Sciences]] (LUMS). A [[research scientist]] in the field of [[superstring theory]] at the [[National Center for Physics]],<ref name="reddiarypk.wordpress.com">{{cite web|url=http://reddiarypk.wordpress.com/2009/10/06/faheem-hussain-lal-salam/ |title=Faheem Hussain – Lal Salam! " Red Diary |publisher=Reddiarypk.wordpress.com |date=6 October 2009 |accessdate=14 December 2010}}</ref> Hussain made contributions to the fields of superstring and [[string theory]]. He was the first Pakistani physicist to publish a research paper in the field of superstring theory.<ref name="pakistaniat.com">{{cite web |url=http://pakistaniat.com/2009/10/04/faheem-hussain/comment-page-2/ |title=Remembering Prof. Faheem Hussain (1942–2009) : ALL THINGS PAKISTAN |publisher=Pakistaniat.com |date=5 October 2009 |accessdate=14 December 2010 |archive-date=1 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121001213740/http://pakistaniat.com/2009/10/04/faheem-hussain/comment-page-2/ |url-status=live }}</ref> A social activist and democratic activist, he authored various scientific research papers in peer-reviewed journals.<ref name="pakistaniat.com"/>

==Education and early life==
Faheem Hussain was born in [[Yavatmal]], Maharashtra, [[British India]] in 1942.{{Citation needed|date= May 2022}} His family moved to [[West Pakistan]] shortly before the [[Partition of India]] on 14 August 1947. He graduated from [[St. Anthony's High School, Lahore]], in 1955 and then enrolled in [[Forman Christian College]].<ref name=LUMS_SSE>{{cite web
 |last         = University
 |first        = LUMS
 |title        = The LUMS SSE Virtual Program Development Team (VPDT)
 |url          = http://sse.lums.edu.pk/vpdt.htm#faheemhussain
 |access-date  = 24 November 2009
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120806193506/http://sse.lums.edu.pk/vpdt.htm#faheemhussain
 |archive-date = 6 August 2012
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |last         = Hoodbhoy
 |first        = Pervez
 |authorlink   = Pervaiz Hoobhoy
 |title        = Reckoning Time for HEC
 |work         = dawa-i-dil
 |publisher    = Chowk.com
 |url          = http://www.chowk.com/interacts/14920/1/0/64
 |access-date  = 24 November 2009
 |archive-url  = https://archive.today/20120320093602/http://www.chowk.com/interacts/14920/1/0/64
 |archive-date = 20 March 2012
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref>
After receiving his double [[Bachelor of Science|BSc(Hons)]] in Mathematics and [[Physics]] from [[Forman Christian College]] in 1960, he moved to the Great Britain.{{Citation needed|date= May 2022}} There, he attended [[Chelsea College of Art and Design|Chelsea College]], London, and completed another B.S. (hons) in physics in 1963. He attended [[Imperial College, London]] where physicist Abdus Salam was also teaching. He began working with Abdus Salam's group at the Imperial College. He completed his MSc in physics from [[Imperial College, London]] under Abdus Salam, and followed by his PhD in [[Theoretical physics]] under the supervision of theoretical [[particle physicist]] [[Paul Taunton Matthews|Paul Matthews]] in 1966.<ref>{{Citation
  | last = Dutta
  | first = Rinku
  | title = Faheem Hussain – Lal Salam!
  | url = http://reddiarypk.wordpress.com/2009/10/06/faheem-hussain-lal-salam/
  | accessdate = 24 November 2009
  | date = 6 October 2009
  | archive-date = 27 December 2009
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20091227162753/http://reddiarypk.wordpress.com/2009/10/06/faheem-hussain-lal-salam/
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref>

==Academic career==

He taught at [[Garyounis University]], [[Benghazi]], [[Libya]], from 1977 to 1979. In 1985 joined Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron, better known as [[DESY]], in Germany. Prior to this, Hussain moved to [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]] and joined the European Organization for Nuclear Research ([[CERN]]). He had also been a visiting professor at the [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]], Germany.<ref name=cern-obit/>

===Support for democracy in Pakistan===
After the Coup d'état by General [[Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq]], Hussain publicly opposed [[Zia-ul-Haq's Islamization]] of Pakistan and supported democracy in his country.<ref name="thenews.com.pk">{{cite web|url=http://www.thenews.com.pk/daily_detail.asp?id=201191 |accessdate=24 November 2009 |title=The News International: Latest News Breaking, Pakistan News }}{{dead link|date=June 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Hussain left Pakistan in 1989 and joined ICTP at the request of Abdus Salam.<ref>{{Citation
 | last=Khalid
 | first=Rasheed
 | author-link=Khalid Rasheen
 | title=Tribute paid to Dr Faheem
 | newspaper=The News International
 | location=Islamabad, Pakistan
 | date=5 October 2009
 | url=http://www.thenews.com.pk/daily_detail.asp?id=201659
 }}</ref>

==Return to Pakistan==
Hussain worked as a senior staff scientist at [[ICTP]] from 1990 then took his retirement and returned to Pakistan in 2004.<ref name="reddiarypk.wordpress.com"/><ref name="thenews.com.pk"/> There, he joined the physics research institute, the [[National Center for Physics]].<ref name="reddiarypk.wordpress.com"/>

==Personal life==
Hussain was married to Jane Steinfels Hussain,<ref name=cern-obit /> an [[United States|American]] woman, from 1968 to 1986.{{citation needed|date=August 2015}}  He later married Sara Monticone Hussain.<ref name=cern-obit />

==Death==
Hussain was suffering from [[prostate cancer]] and died on 29 September 2009.<ref name=cern-obit>{{cite web |title=Obituaries: Faheem Hussain 1942–2009 |url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/41016 |publisher=[[CERN]] |accessdate=2 August 2015 |work=CERN Courier |date=7 December 2009 |archive-date=21 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100921135725/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/41016 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was widely respected by his colleagues, collaborators and students, for both his academic brilliance and principled stance on ideals of democracy and freedom of speech.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-10-29 |title=Remembering an icon |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/841259/remembering-an-icon |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=DAWN.COM |language=en}}</ref>
